name: Deux Cents
description: Deux Cents (Two Hundred) is a point-trick card game popular in New Brunswick, Canada. Players bid for the right to choose trumps and try to win tricks containing point cards (Aces, Tens, and Fives). The game is said to be of French Acadian origin and is closely related to Rook.

overview.description: Deux Cents (Two Hundred) is a point-trick card game popular in New Brunswick, Canada. Players bid for the right to choose trumps and try to win tricks containing point cards (Aces, Tens, and Fives). The game is said to be of French Acadian origin and is closely related to Rook.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: New Brunswick, Canada
Time Period: At least 1930s or earlier
Historical Development: French Acadian game, possibly related to Rook (1906) or sharing a common ancestor
Cultural Significance: Important social game in New Brunswick, played for 3-4 generations
timeline: 1930s or earlier: Game already established in New Brunswick
1906: Rook published by Parker Brothers - possible connection or shared ancestor
Mid-20th century: Spread to Quebec (as Le Rough, Le Ruff, La Bloutte, La Fouine)
Present: Played in New Brunswick, Quebec, Maine (USA), and Alberta
history.cultural: Deux Cents represents an important part of French Acadian cultural heritage in Canada. The game brings communities together and has been passed down through families for generations.
history.evolution: The game spread from New Brunswick throughout Atlantic Canada and into Quebec. Various names and rules developed regionally. Related to Chinese games Sheng Ji (particularly 100), though historical connection is uncertain.

setup.players:
Minimum Players: 4
Maximum Players: 4
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West)
setup.deck:
Type: Modified 36-card pack
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
Cards removed: All 2s, 3s, 4s, and 6s
Card ranking: A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-5
setup.dealing:
First dealer chosen at random (often by dealing for first jack)
Deal passes clockwise after each hand
9 cards to each player in batches of three
Cards shuffled by dealer and cut by player to dealer's right
setup.equipment:
36-card modified deck
Score sheet
Table space for tricks

rules.objective: Be the first partnership to reach 200 points (or other agreed target). Points come from capturing Aces (10 pts), Tens (10 pts), and Fives (5 pts) in tricks.
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal 9 cards to each player
2. Bidding begins left of dealer, continues clockwise
3. Minimum bid 50, multiples of 5, must be higher than last bid
4. Bidding continues until 3 players pass or someone bids 100 (maximum)
5. Highest bidder (contractor) announces trump suit
6. Contractor leads to first trick
7. Must follow suit if able; may play any card if unable
8. Highest trump wins if trumps played; otherwise highest of led suit
9. Winner leads to next trick
10. After all cards played, count points in tricks
keyRules: If contractor fails to announce trump before leading, suit of first card played becomes trump
Opponents with 100+ who both passed score nothing for that hand
Score can go negative (shown in box or 'in the hole')

strategy.basic:
Count points in your hand (Aces, Tens, Fives worth 25 points each)
Bid based on strength of hand and support from partner
Follow suit when required
Try to capture opponents' point cards
strategy.intermediate:
Evaluate partner's strength through bidding
Use 'cutting' (trumping) strategically when unable to follow
Discard point cards on partner's winning tricks
Block opponents from making their bid
strategy.advanced:
Sophisticated bidding with partner communication
Card counting to track remaining point cards
Defensive play to set opponents' contract
Endgame strategy when approaching 200 points
tips: Consider your partner's potential strength when bidding
Don't overbid - failing a contract costs the full bid amount
Save trumps for when you need to win crucial tricks
Watch for opportunities to discard point cards on partner's tricks
If opponents are close to 200, bid aggressively to stop them
